A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sparse-RL research and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. All 14 pages support comparison; the appendix pages are identical.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments, sparse-inference evaluations, training diagnostics, and a KV-budget ablation in Tables 1–2, Figures 1–6, and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark results, sparse-inference evaluations, training diagnostics, and ablation results reported in v1.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same sparse rollout procedure, sequence rejection rule, importance reweighting, and Sparse-RL objective. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions train on the SimpleRL-Zoo hard split and evaluate the same seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks. The sparse-inference scenario in Section 5.4 and benchmark coverage in Appendix B are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the base models, dense GRPO, and naive sparse GRPO with R-KV and SnapKV. Table 2 retains the same comparison between dense-trained and Sparse-RL-trained models under sparse inference.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendices A–B retain the same model configurations, sample sizes, hyperparameters, 400-step training budget, and 512-token main KV budget. Avg@32, Pass@1, sparse-inference settings, and the budget-sweep protocol are unchanged.

E4.justification: The training-dynamics analyses, sparse-inference evaluation, KV-budget ablation, rejection/clipping diagnostics in Appendix C, and anomalous-sequence example in Appendix F are all retained without revision.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing sampled-response averaging and training-curve reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted curves, and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same Qwen2.5-1.5B average scores of 36.2 for Sparse-RL with R-KV and 35.4 for dense GRPO in both versions.

T1.justification: The policy definitions, importance-ratio decomposition, rejection criterion, objectives, and gradient derivations remain unchanged, including Equations 1–17 and Appendices D–E.

C1.justification: The claims about stable sparse rollouts, memory savings, near-dense performance, and sparse-inference robustness remain unchanged. The introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain their original scope.

C2.justification: The interpretations of compression noise, policy adaptation, and budget sensitivity are unchanged. Both versions retain the same limitations concerning task generalization and the sampling-efficiency trade-off.

D1.justification: V2 adds an abstract statement that training data and code are publicly available, with a footnote pointing to the RUCKBReasoning/Sparse-RL repository. V1 lacks this project-access information; existing implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning are unchanged. The new project repository footnote supplies access information without revising the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: V2 adds one resource-availability sentence and its footnote, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added sentence and repository footnote cause modest column/page reflow: dataset footnotes move from page 5 to page 6, and the conclusion extends onto page 9. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–3 retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: V2 supplies a concrete code-and-training-data repository pointer absent from v1, modestly improving resource discovery and reproducibility documentation. The scientific content and appendices are unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents or usability.
